static_checks_1.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Combines four sub-scores, averaged 1:1:1:1, into a single check. First, workbook structure: opens /logs/agent/authorization_tracker.xlsx with openpyxl, confirms a sheet named conditions_register and a sheet named sponsor_readiness exist, and for each sheet counts how many of its required column headers are present (15 for conditions_register, 7 for sponsor_readiness); scores the mean of the two per-sheet header ratios, 0.0 for a missing/unreadable sheet. Second, unit coverage: reads the unit_id column of both sheets, scores the mean of the two per-sheet ratios of distinct recognised unit_ids to the 20 expected, then subtracts a penalty of up to 0.5 per sheet for duplicate unit_ids and up to 0.5 for unit_ids outside CR-01..CR-20; blank rows are ignored rather than counted as coverage. Third, briefing presence: confirms /logs/agent/legislative_briefing.md exists and counts its words -- at or above 150 words scores 1.0, below 150 scores half the word ratio, missing/unreadable scores 0.0. Fourth, document_relationship coheres with related_unit_id across the 20 units, where supplemental requires a different in-cohort unit_id and base requires not_stated; for any unit whose own report names itself as a supplement to an earlier Chief's Report (a specific phrase pattern, not a bare substring search for 'supplement'), plain internal coherence is not enough -- that unit must actually be marked supplemental with a valid related_unit_id, so declaring every row 'base' cannot pass this sub-score on self-consistency alone, and the reverse direction is checked too when the packaged reports are readable (a unit marked 'supplemental' whose own report carries none of that self-declaration language does not earn coherence credit either). These four are folded into one registry slot, rather than three static checks plus a document_relationship sub-ratio buried in the cross-artifact check, because all four are satisfiable by a submission that never reads a single report -- the workbook can have the right shape, the right unit_ids, a long-enough briefing, and a uniform 'base' column with no genuine per-report reading behind any of it. All checks carry equal weight in the final reward, so this one registry slot counts the same as any check that actually requires source-grounded content -- the substantive checks outnumbering the structural ones is what keeps reward from being dominated by shape alone, not a smaller weight on this slot.
static_checks_1.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Blocks a submission that writes the wrong shape entirely (a CSV, a flat sheet, invented columns), covers only a handful of reports padded with repeats, ships an empty or one-line briefing, or declares every document_relationship 'base' with related_unit_id=not_stated everywhere -- all shape-level shortcuts that require no reading of the twenty signed reports -- while keeping their combined weight in the overall reward proportionate to how little genuine work they demand.

reward_hacking_checks_1.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Checks five enum columns across the 20 units: project_purpose, benefit_basis and document_relationship in conditions_register, sponsor_named and readiness_label in sponsor_readiness. readiness_label additionally loses credit for a row when the packaged reports are readable and the unit has a real, non-placeholder project_name or nonfederal_sponsor, but neither one is grounded in that unit's own report text: readiness_label is a judgment call this check cannot verify directly without risking false negatives on a legitimate judgment, but a categorization is not a finding at all when the row it is attached to never identified the unit in the first place. sponsor_named is checked the same way in the other direction: a 'yes' value is format-valid regardless of whether the paired nonfederal_sponsor is a real name or an invented one, so when the packaged reports are readable a 'yes' cell additionally requires that nonfederal_sponsor be grounded in that unit's own report, closing the gap where a fabricated but well-formed sponsor name earned the same format credit as a genuinely identified one. Denominator is 100 cells. A cell scores when its value is exactly one of the allowed values for that column. Then, for every enum column except document_relationship, if one value occupies 90 percent or more of the 20 rows (55 percent or more for benefit_basis specifically, see below), all credit already awarded for that value in that column is withdrawn; and separately, if the column's values follow an exact repeating cycle of period 2 to 8 across all 20 rows (round-robin filling instead of a single bulk value), all credit for that column is withdrawn as well. document_relationship stays exempt because at most a couple of reports in a twenty report cohort are supplemental, so a near constant column there is expected rather than suspicious. sponsor_named is not exempt from a separate, direct guard: because every signed Chief's Report is produced for a project that has a cost-sharing sponsor, if half or more of the 20 sponsor_named cells are anything other than yes, credit for those cells is withdrawn regardless of variety, on the theory that a real read of these reports finds a named sponsor far more often than not; padding that still manages to name a sponsor is caught instead by reward_hacking_checks_4, which requires sponsor_named=yes to agree substantively with a real nonfederal_sponsor value. A non-periodic, well-varied assignment of project_purpose or benefit_basis still defeats both of the above patterns while remaining pure guesswork, so for the categories with standard, near-universal USACE terminology (project_purpose's five concrete categories; benefit_basis's NED, NER and LPP) credit for that cell is separately withdrawn, when the packaged reports are readable, unless the relevant part of that unit's own report text contains at least one of the phrases a report actually about that category would use. project_purpose is checked against only the opening transmittal sentence (up to the first occurrence of 'accompanied'), not the whole document, because the same or next paragraph routinely cites a generic authorizing statute naming several unrelated categories ('... in the interest of navigation, flood control, water supply, and related purposes ...') that would otherwise let almost any of the five categories pass for almost any report regardless of its actual purpose. benefit_basis has an analogous problem verified across all twenty packaged reports -- 'National Economic Development' is named in nearly every report's general evaluation-criteria language regardless of which basis this specific project used, and a report that explicitly deviates from NED (a policy exception) still contains that literal phrase -- so NED/NER/LPP are checked only in the window right after 'The Recommended Plan is/consists of/includes ...', where these reports reliably state their own answer, and a plain negation cue there ('is not', 'not the', 'deviate', 'policy exception') means the match does not count. benefit_basis's other catch-all-like values (TNB, combined, not_stated) are deliberately left unchecked by the phrase test because this cohort's own reports show a genuinely high rate of non-NED plans and no single reliable phrase exists for a catch-all; non_NED specifically is checked without that risk, since every non_NED case found in this cohort explicitly carries a negation cue in that same window, so a non_NED claim with no such cue there is not corroborated by the report. Because a catch-all value cannot be phrase-bound, benefit_basis alone uses a lowered 55 percent bulk-fill threshold instead of the default 90 percent: verified against this cohort's own reports, even NED, the single most common genuine basis, appears in well under half of them, so 55 percent still leaves ample room for honest work while catching a dominant catch-all value (e.g. 'combined' bulk-filled across most rows) that would otherwise clear the default threshold untouched. Catch-all categories (multiple, other, not_stated, TNB, non_NED, combined) have no single reliable phrase and are left unchecked by this phrase test; because that would let an assignment dodge the phrase test entirely by leaning on catch-all values, project_purpose additionally loses credit for all of its catch-all cells once they reach a quarter or more of the 20 rows -- a low bar deliberately, since every one of this cohort's twenty reports independently verified states a concrete purpose in its own subject line and a couple of catch-all rows is the most a genuinely ambiguous case should need. document_relationship's uniformity exemption is not a blanket pass either: when the packaged reports are readable, a unit whose own report names itself as a supplement to an earlier Chief's Report in its own subject line or opening self-declaration (checked with a specific phrase pattern, not a bare substring search for the word 'supplement', which also matches unrelated uses like 'a supplemental NEPA document' or 'supplemented by bathymetry data' and was verified against all twenty packaged reports to avoid exactly that false-positive) but whose row calls it 'base' loses credit for that cell.
reward_hacking_checks_1.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Blocks null and default padding, invented enum wording, and the bulk fill shortcut of writing one plausible value such as not_stated or flood_risk_management down an entire column without reading the reports.

reward_hacking_checks_2.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Parses the citations cell of each conditions_register row and the supporting_citation cell of each sponsor_readiness row. Entries are split on the pipe character and each must match the form CR-NN page N. A citation counts only when the cited unit_id equals the row's own unit_id and the page number is at least 1 and, when the packaged reports are readable, no greater than that report's real page count. conditions_register needs 2 distinct valid citations to earn its half point, sponsor_readiness needs 1. instruction.md requires the citations cell to support both recommended_plan and estimated_first_cost, so both are bound: when estimated_first_cost is a real, non-placeholder value and the packaged reports are readable, the register row earns nothing for that sheet unless at least one cited page's own extracted text contains that cost figure's digit sequence, and separately, when recommended_plan is a real, non-placeholder value, the row earns nothing unless at least one cited page contains one of recommended_plan's distinctive (non-generic, stopword-filtered) words -- a citation that does not do the job the instruction names it for is not a weaker citation, so it is not worth half credit for correct formatting alone. sponsor_readiness's supporting_citation has no single field it must support the same way, so instead it earns nothing unless at least one cited page names that unit's own project_name or nonfederal_sponsor (whichever is a real, non-placeholder value) -- binding to those identifiers rather than to a specific readiness narrative avoids penalising a legitimate paraphrase of sponsor_obligations that does not repeat the source's exact wording. Separately, on each sheet independently, if 90 percent or more of the 20 rows cite the exact same set of page numbers, credit for those rows on that sheet is withdrawn as same-page filler, since twenty independently read reports of different lengths essentially never collapse onto one identical citation set. Denominator is 20 units, half a point per sheet. Page-range and content binding are skipped and noted when /input_artifacts/chiefs_reports is not visible; unit binding and format still apply.
reward_hacking_checks_2.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Stops an agent from pasting one plausible citation string (or one fixed page set) across every row, from citing another unit's report to support this unit's numbers, from inventing page numbers that the signed report does not have, and from citing a page that never actually contains the cost figure it is supposed to support.

reward_hacking_checks_3.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Examines seven narrative columns across 20 units for a denominator of 140 cells: recommended_plan, environmental_commitments, implementation_dependencies and authorization_matters in conditions_register, sponsor_obligations, readiness_rationale and outstanding_dependency in sponsor_readiness (outstanding_dependency is graded here, not only referenced as evidence for reward_hacking_checks_6, since instruction.md requires it to name the single item most likely to hold that project up and nothing else scored whether it actually does). A cell scores 1 when its whitespace and punctuation normalised text is unique among the 20 rows of that column, meets a per-column minimum length, does not share a template with even one other row once that row's own unit_id, project_name and any bare numbers are stripped out of the text before comparison (catching both a boilerplate sentence with only the identifier swapped per row and a small fixed bank of clauses cycled by row index with only a per-row index number or identifier changing, either of which plain verbatim-duplicate detection would score as twenty distinct cells), and, when the packaged reports are readable, contains at least one specific non-generic word (a place, agency, statute or engineering feature name, filtered against a broad stopword list of vocabulary common to any Corps report narrative) that actually occurs somewhere in that unit's own report text -- distinctness alone does not require truth, so twenty different fabricated-but-varied sentences would otherwise still score as twenty genuine summaries. Cells that are empty or an explicit not_stated marker are excluded from the numerator without being counted as duplicates.
reward_hacking_checks_3.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Blocks the boilerplate shortcut of writing one generic sentence about sponsor obligations or environmental commitments and repeating it down the column, which reads as complete but reflects no per-report reading.

reward_hacking_checks_4.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Scores the mean of up to four sub-ratios. First, sponsor_named substantively agrees with nonfederal_sponsor across the 20 units: only a row with a real, non-placeholder nonfederal_sponsor value paired with sponsor_named=yes counts as agreement; a row where both cells are not_stated/no is internally coherent but earns nothing, since it carries no finding to be consistent about, and when the packaged reports are readable that nonfederal_sponsor value must also be grounded in that unit's own report -- a fabricated but well-formed sponsor name must not pass just because it is present and paired with yes. Second, when the packaged reports are readable, project_name must contain at least one distinctive (non-generic) word that actually occurs in that unit's own report text -- a check against the source rather than against the agent's own other artifact, since a wholesale invented name can otherwise be made to agree with itself across both sheets and the briefing for free. Third, every unit_id the briefing names is accompanied by that unit's exact register project_name, and, when the packaged reports are readable, that project_name must independently pass the same source-grounding test as the second sub-ratio -- agreement between the briefing and the register alone no longer counts if the name they agree on is fabricated. Fourth, for every readiness_label the sheet actually assigns, the briefing must mention that label within 400 characters of a unit_id that actually carries it, and, when the packaged reports are readable, that unit's project_name must also be source-grounded -- a label discussion anchored to a fabricated project earns nothing. (document_relationship/related_unit_id coherence, formerly a fifth sub-ratio here, now lives in static_checks_1 alongside the other shape-level checks it is satisfiable alongside.)
reward_hacking_checks_4.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Stops the sheets and briefing being produced independently and contradicting each other, stops a briefing that name-drops unit_ids it never analysed, stops a padded submission earning consistency credit for agreeing that everything is not_stated, and stops a keyword dump of the four readiness category names from passing as discussion of them.

reward_hacking_checks_5.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Selects 6 units by fixed stride at offset 0 over the sorted unit list (reward_hacking_checks_6 uses offset 1, so the two LLM-judged checks in this file source-verify 12 distinct units between them, not the same 6 twice), reads each unit's own packaged report text, and asks the judge to score that unit's submitted register row against that report text on 7 criteria: project_name, nonfederal_sponsor and report_date accuracy, whether recommended_plan describes what the report recommends, whether the three narrative columns are traceable to statements in that report, whether project_purpose actually matches what the report's plan is for, and whether benefit_basis matches the plan formulation basis the report states or implies rather than an arbitrary or rotating enum pick. Per unit score is supported_criteria over 7; check score is the mean over the 6 sampled units, with an unreturned unit counted as 0. Agent text is delimited as untrusted and the judge is told to ignore instructions inside it. Temperature 0, one retry on unparseable JSON. A missing WANDB_API_KEY, an unavailable requests library, a failed call or unreadable source reports produce an explicit infrastructure error and score 0.0.
reward_hacking_checks_5.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Catches fluent rows that were written from general Corps practice rather than from the specific signed report, which every deterministic check on this sheet would otherwise accept because the format and enums are correct.

reward_hacking_checks_6.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Supplies the judge with unit_id, project_name, readiness_label and outstanding_dependency for all 20 units as the briefing's evidence base (labelled to the judge as the agent's own submitted claims, not independent evidence), plus, for a fixed 6-unit stride sample at offset 1 (reward_hacking_checks_5 uses offset 0, so between the two checks 12 distinct units get source-verified, not the same 6 twice) with readable source, that unit's own signed-report excerpt (up to 2500 characters), labelled as authoritative and independent of the submitted rows -- without this, a briefing that is fluently consistent with a fabricated register row had no way to be caught, since the judge's only evidence was the agent's own claims about itself. Scores 6 criteria at 0, 1 or 2 each: the sponsor action question, the technical clarification question, the federal advocacy question, recurring portfolio obligations, whether the briefing states plainly where the reports do not settle a question, and source_grounded -- whether the briefing's discussion of the sampled units is actually consistent with those units' own signed-report excerpts (not merely with the submitted register rows). Scored 1 (neutral) only when no excerpts were available at all -- if excerpts WERE available but the briefing avoids naming any of the sampled units, that scores 0, not neutral, since a briefing that names every other project but never the ones this check can source-verify is evasive, not merely unassessed. When excerpts were available and source_grounded comes back 0 for either reason, the other five criteria -- which are only ever graded against the agent's own submitted rows, not independent evidence, so a fabricated-but-internally-consistent register-and-briefing pair could otherwise clear all five at full credit purely by agreeing with itself -- are capped at their thin/loosely-tied tier (1 point each) rather than allowed to still claim the fully-verified tier (2 points each) they were never independently checked for. For the first five criteria, 2 requires reasoning clearly and specifically drawn from that project's own register row; 1 requires named projects with reasoning that is at least genuinely (if thinly) tied to that project's own evidence; 0 covers an absent criterion or boilerplate -- a templated sentence with only the identifier swapped, the same generic reasoning reused across different projects, or an assertion that does not engage with that project's own outstanding_dependency or readiness_label -- and the judge is explicitly told that being asserted at all is not itself worth partial credit, since an earlier looser wording of the '1' tier let confident-sounding but fabricated boilerplate clear it for every criterion. Check score is the total over 12. Temperature 0. A missing WANDB_API_KEY or failed call produces an explicit infrastructure error and score 0.0.
reward_hacking_checks_6.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Blocks a briefing that stuffs every rubric term and readiness category into generic prose without tying any of them to named projects, and blocks a confident briefing that papers over questions the twenty reports leave open.

partial_oracle_checks_1.detailed_explanation_of_checks: Loads the sampled units from tests/partial_oracle.json and iterates the expected unit keys, so a unit the agent omitted scores 0 for its fields rather than being skipped. For each declared field, compares the submitted conditions_register value: report_date by digit sequence so date formatting does not matter, enum columns by exact case-insensitive value, free-text columns by normalised equality or by containment where the shorter side carries at least two tokens, so a bare generic word cannot match a fuller sponsor name. Score is matched fields over compared fields. A missing, unparseable or empty oracle, or an oracle with no comparable fields, is an infrastructure error scoring 0.0. estimated_first_cost and benefit_basis are deliberately excluded from this comparison because the reports state several first-cost figures and sometimes two plan bases; cost is bound to source in partial_oracle_checks_2 instead.
partial_oracle_checks_1.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Gives an independently hand-verified anchor for a sample of units, so a submission that is internally consistent and correctly formatted but factually invented cannot pass on shape alone.

partial_oracle_checks_2.detailed_explanation_of_checks: For each of the 20 units, extracts the digit sequence of estimated_first_cost and requires it to (a) exactly match one of that unit's own report's tokenised 3-or-more-digit number runs (thousands separators removed, but the match is membership in that token set, not a substring search over the whole report's digits concatenated together, which would let an arbitrary invented figure match almost any sufficiently long report by chance) and (b) occur within a 180-character window of some mention of the word 'cost' in that report -- membership alone does not require the matched number to have anything to do with cost, since a page number, a phone number or another figure can coincide with an invented cost by chance in a multi-page report; the bare word 'cost' is used as the proximity cue rather than a longer phrase like 'first cost' or 'total cost' because these reports vary in which cost label they use for the recommended plan's own figure. Also requires the normalised cost_price_level string to occur in that unit's own report text. Denominator is 40 cells. Any first-cost figure the report actually states near a cost mention is accepted, because these reports commonly state a total, an initial construction figure and a periodic nourishment figure. A value written not_stated earns no credit and is reported for trainer review. Unreadable source reports produce an explicit infrastructure error and score 0.0.
partial_oracle_checks_2.how_it_prevents_task_authenticity_violat: Binds the two most fabricable numeric fields to the canonical record and field rather than to global source text, so a figure copied from another unit's report, rounded, converted to a different price year, or invented outright earns nothing.
